issues.description: The UML and problem text indicate Animal and its concrete subclasses should have constructors that initialize the class attributes (the UML shows only a name attribute). The template's example Main uses single-argument constructors (e.g. Seal("Clarabelle")). However, the solution repository defines constructors that take two parameters (String name, int age) for Animal, Seal, Pig, and Goat. This mismatch between the expected single-argument constructors (name-only) and the two-argument constructors in the solution can confuse students about which constructor signature to implement and prevents direct use of the example code in Main.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent with the UML/problem text. Either (A) remove the extra age parameter from the solution classes and provide single-argument constructors (String name) for Animal, Seal, Pig, Goat to match the UML and the example Main; or (B) update the problem statement and UML to document the additional 'age' attribute and require two-argument constructors (String name, int age). Prefer option A to match the current UML and template examples.

issues.description: The UML and problem description list Animal as having only a 'name' attribute (and require getter/setter for it). The solution's Animal class adds an extra 'age' attribute and corresponding getters/setters. This introduces an attribute-type/structure mismatch between the specification and the solution: students guided by the UML/problem text would not expect or be required to implement an 'age' attribute, while the solution includes it.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the data model with the UML/problem text. Either remove the 'age' attribute and related methods from the solution's Animal class so it only contains 'name', or update the UML/problem statement to include 'age' as a required attribute and explicitly require constructors/getters/setters for it. Prefer removing 'age' from the solution to avoid contradicting the provided UML and example usages.

issues.description: Representation of the Animal entity is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement (UML) and the template Main usage imply Animal (and its subclasses Seal/Pig/Goat) have only a name and are instantiated with a single String argument, while the solution adds an additional 'age' attribute and requires constructors with (String name, int age). This mismatch makes it unclear to students which constructor/signature they should implement and how many attributes the Animal class must have.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the Animal API across artifacts. Either (A) remove the extra 'age' attribute from the solution and provide single-argument constructors (String name) for Animal and its subclasses so they match the UML and the template Main usage; or (B) update the problem statement and template Main to include the 'age' attribute and show/expect constructors with (String name, int age). Prefer option A to match the provided UML which specifies only 'name'.
